interface.title: GeoResistivity — Apparent Resistivity Calculator
interface.field: Near-surface geophysics / electrical resistivity (vertical electrical sounding, Schlumberger array)
interface.stage_of_work: Field data entry, quality control, reduction to apparent resistivity, and reporting of VES soundings
interface.what_it_is_for: Turning raw VES field readings (ΔV, I, electrode spacings or K) into unit-checked apparent resistivities with quality warnings, a log-log sounding curve, CSV exports and a PDF/HTML report.

data.note: I typed single measurements in by hand. I uploaded sample_measurements.csv (8 rows, comma separator, decimal point) into Single measurements, and synthetic_ves_excel_pt_br.csv (38 rows, ';' separator, decimal comma, both detected automatically) into the Field sheet. I switched the interface from Portuguese to English through the sidebar Language selector. The number format stayed pt-BR (decimal comma) throughout.

tree.general: Reduce resistivity field readings to apparent resistivity, check their quality, and share the results
tree.specific: Compute ρa = K·ΔV/I for Schlumberger VES readings, build the log-log VES curve, and export CSVs, a figure and a VES report

features.name: Unit-aware single-reading calculator with geometry-derived constant
features.general: Enter a measured signal, a source strength and an instrument constant, each with its own unit. Either type the constant or have it computed from the geometry. Get the derived quantity, the SI-converted inputs, and a warning when the geometry is poor.
features.specific: Single measurement form: radio Enter K / Calculate K (Schlumberger); ΔV with mV/V unit, I with A/mA/µA, K or AB/2 and MN with length units; 'Calculate and add measurement' shows ρa, a Converted values expander, and the 'MN is wide' warning.
steps: choose Enter K or Calculate K (Schlumberger)
type ΔV, I and K (or AB/2 and MN) and pick each unit
press Calculate and add measurement
read ρa and expand Converted values; read any quality warning
serves_tasks: Enter one reading with a known geometric factor and read the result with converted units
Enter a reading and let the tool compute the geometric factor from electrode spacing
Flag an unreliable electrode geometry when computing a reading

features.name: Multi-array geometric factor calculator
features.general: Pick a sensor layout from a list. The input fields change to that layout's distances, and the tool computes the layout constant to copy into a measurement.
features.specific: K calculator expander: Array dropdown plus Length unit. Schlumberger (AB/2+MN), Wenner-α (a) and General four-electrode (AM, BM, AN, BN) were used; Dipole-dipole and Pole-dipole (remote B) are listed but their forms were never opened. 'Calculate K' shows K and a hint to use it with Enter K.
steps: expand K calculator
choose the array and length unit
type the spacings shown for that array
press Calculate K and copy the value into Enter K
serves_tasks: Compute a geometric factor for other electrode arrays

features.name: Session measurement log with spacing plot
features.general: Collect computed results in a running table. Plot them against a distance on linear or log-log axes, with optional sorting. Undo the last entry, clear all, or export.
features.specific: Session Measurements dataframe + Remove last measurement / Clear all measurements (not tried) / Export CSV + Spacing Plot with Scale Linear/Log-log and 'Sort by AB/2 for visualization' (the table keeps acquisition order).
steps: add measurements (by hand or by import)
toggle Linear or Log-log
tick Sort by AB/2
press Remove last measurement if an entry is wrong
press Export CSV
serves_tasks: Review the session table, plot results against spacing, and remove a mistaken entry
Export the computed measurements as a table file

features.name: CSV import wizard with format detection and column mapping
features.general: Upload a delimited file. The tool detects the separator, encoding and decimal mark and previews the rows. Map each file column to a required field, set units for unit-less columns, see how many rows are valid, then import into a chosen target, either replacing or appending.
features.specific: Import CSV tab: Separator Detect; preview table; Import into Field sheet / Single measurements; Columns mapping dropdowns (ΔV*, I*, K*, AB/2, MN, units, Marker, Excluded, Exclusion reason); Decimal separator 'Detect from the numbers'; Units for columns without a unit column; 'N of N rows ready to import'; How: Replace / Add after (only Replace was used); Import N rows. Both test files parsed fully, so the listing of problem rows was never shown.
steps: upload the CSV
check the detected separator and decimal mark in the summary line
choose Import into and check the column mapping and units
choose Replace the field sheet or Add after the current rows
press Import N rows and read the confirmation
serves_tasks: Load a table of measurements, check the column mapping and parsing, and append them
Load a regional-format field sheet file and replace the current sheet with it

features.name: Locale-aware numeric input
features.general: Accept numbers typed or imported with either a decimal comma or a decimal point, and show results in the chosen regional number format.
features.specific: Typed values such as 120,5 and 0,08 were accepted in the Single measurement form, and the import wizard detected decimal comma vs decimal point per file ('Detect from the numbers (Comma (1,5))'). Rejection of ambiguous values (e.g. 1,000) and per-field error messages were never triggered in this run.
steps: type a value with decimal comma or point, or upload a file
check the detected decimal mark in the import summary
read the results shown in the chosen number format
serves_tasks: Enter one reading with a known geometric factor and read the result with converted units
Load a regional-format field sheet file and replace the current sheet with it

features.name: Editable field sheet with repeat aggregation and CV quality check
features.general: Type or correct readings in a spreadsheet grid that has per-row exclude flags and reasons. Readings at the same position are pooled into mean, standard error and coefficient of variation. A position is flagged when its CV exceeds a limit.
features.specific: Field sheet grid (Marker, AB/2, MN, ΔV, I, Exclude, Exclusion reason) with ΔV/I unit selectors and a CV limit [%] stepper. The positions table shows K, Readings '2 (+1 excluded)', ρa, ρa standard error, CV [%] and Warnings 'CV above limit'. Seen in use: pooling of an imported repeat, an exclusion that came in from the file, and a ΔV edit raising the CV warning. Not done: ticking Exclude and typing a reason, adding a repeat row by hand, changing the CV limit.
steps: import or open a field sheet with repeated positions
read the positions table: Readings, standard error, CV and Warnings
edit ΔV or I in a row and press Enter
read the updated CV and any 'CV above limit' warning
serves_tasks: Inspect the readings, including overlap, repeated and excluded readings
Read per-position results: geometric factor, number of readings, mean, standard error, variability
Correct a reading and see the variability warning respond

features.name: Segmented log-log sounding curve with error bars and warning markers
features.general: Plot the derived value against a distance on log-log axes, with one coloured segment per secondary-spacing group. Show ±1 standard-error bars where readings were repeated, and ring the points that carry quality warnings.
features.specific: Vertical Electrical Sounding (Schlumberger) chart: one colour per MN (0,5 / 2 / 5 / 20 / 50 / 100 m), 'Error bars (±1 standard error)' toggle, red 'Quality warning' ring on flagged positions.
steps: fill or import the field sheet
toggle Error bars
read the curve and the overlap segments
spot ringed points flagged in the positions table
serves_tasks: View the log-log curve split by receiver spacing, with error bars
Correct a reading and see the variability warning respond

features.name: Change history with undo and CSV audit export
features.general: Each correction to entered data is logged with its time, row and old→new value. The last change can be undone (the undo is logged too), and the log can be exported.
features.specific: Change history expander: '1 change recorded. Undo reverts: ΔV 10,5220 → 15'; Undo last change; Show filter (All changes); table No./Time/Row/Change; Export history (CSV).
steps: edit a value in the field sheet
expand Change history and read the entry
press Undo last change
press Export history (CSV)
serves_tasks: Review, undo and export the audit trail of edits

features.name: Print-scale figure export
features.general: Export the plot as a raster or vector file at a standard size, or at a fixed physical scale (mm per decade) that matches printed log paper, with an optional title.
features.specific: Export figure expander: Format PNG 300 dpi / SVG / PDF (only SVG was used); Size Standard (17.8 × 17.8 cm) or Bilog paper scale with a Modulus [mm per decade] stepper (plot area 15 × 20 cm, 3 × 4 decades); 'Title with VES no., place, and date'; Download figure.
steps: expand Export figure
choose the format
choose Standard or Bilog paper scale and set the modulus
toggle the title and press Download figure
serves_tasks: Export the curve as a print-scale vector figure

features.name: Sounding report generator
features.general: Produce one document that combines survey header, curve, per-position results, readings with exclusions, warnings, change history and methods, in the chosen language and number format, as PDF or HTML.
features.specific: VES report expander: Report format PDF (A4) / HTML → Download report; the HTML holds 'Survey and acquisition details', 'Summary' (36 positions, 37 used, 1 excluded) and an SVG VES curve.
steps: fill Survey details
expand VES report
choose PDF (A4) or HTML
press Download report
serves_tasks: Generate a summary report of the sounding
